_doc: Traffic and pedestrians (spec sim.md §5-§6, Roadcraft src/sim/**). Anti-gridlock (traffic/junctions.ts, micro.ts, regions.ts): jam_seconds/release_every_s jammed-junction release, starve_seconds exit claim, detour_after_s detour at a full exit, reconsider_* route reconsideration in a full queue, bpr_gain congestion cost, tail_credit_* room a moving tail frees, gov_* fleet governor. Signals (CONTRAN MBST vol. V, Res. 483/2014): opposite approaches share a stage, and each stage's green is actuated by the vehicles (cap. 7, green extension, optimum cut): a detection section signal_extension_s[lanes - 1] seconds of travel before the stop line (table 8.1: 4,1 / 1,8 / 1,0 / 0,6 / 0,4 s for 1 to 5 lanes, saturation flow 0,5 ucp/s per lane), each vehicle over it asking for that much more green; the minimum green is the largest of the vehicles' safety green signal_safety_green_s (5.14: never under 10 s), the queue between the section and the line signal_lost_start_s + (distance / signal_queue_spacing_m) x 3600 / signal_sat_flow_lane_h (7.3.1, Eq. 8.2: 3 s, 6 m, 1800 ucp/h per lane) and what the walkers it lets cross need: their safety green ped_safety_green_s (4 s), flashing red ped_reaction_s + crossing length / ped_clear_speed (5.7.2: 1,0 s and 1,2 m/s) and all-red ped_all_red_s (at least 1 s); the maximum green shares out the longest cycle signal_cycle_max_s (5.9: 120 s) left after the intergreens (7.3.3: the flows of a fixed plan are not known beforehand, so the stages get equal shares). The far (meso) traffic asks for green as it leaves a signalled lane, a saturation headway at a time. The intergreen after each green (5.7.1, Eq. 6.4-6.5): amber signal_reaction_s + v / (2 signal_decel) at the regulated speed (t_pr 1,0 s, a_ad 3,0 m/s²), at least amber_min_s up to amber_low_kmh, amber_min_mid_s up to amber_mid_kmh and amber_min_high_s above (3, 4 and 5 s), at most amber_max_s (5 s, the rest goes to the all-red); all-red (d2 + signal_vehicle_m) / v, d2 from the stop line past the junction and the far crosswalk, c 5 m, plus signal_ped_red_s (1 s) when walkers cross in the next stage. At the amber a vehicle stops when it can stop at the line as that timing supposes (reaction, then signal_decel); the others reach the line within the amber. Pedestrians (peds.ts): trips of ped_trip_min_m..max_m between nodes; they cross arms along the middle of the painted zebra and vehicles stop behind the stop line (both from data/catalog/street_furniture.json crossing), walkers step off only with ped_critical_gap_s to spare and give a vehicle standing ped_courtesy_s its turn; ped_span_reach_m = heavy half width + 0.9 m either side of a lane. Walking speeds (Weidmann, Transporttechnik der Fussgänger, IVT ETH Zürich 1993: free speed 1,34 m/s, standard deviation 0,26 m/s): uniform between walk_speed_min and walk_speed_max, the same mean and deviation (1,34 -+ 0,26 x sqrt 3). Crowd (SUMO MSPModel_Striping, sumo.dlr.de/docs/sumo.html pedestrian.striping.*): the footway in ped_stripe_m stripes (stripe-width 0,64 m), a walker's centre at least half a stripe ped_margin_m off its edges (SUMO walks on the middle of its stripe); a body of radius ped_body_m (Fruin, Pedestrian Planning and Design, 1971: body ellipse 18 x 24 in, taken as the circle on its short axis, 0,46 m); a walker looks ped_look_m ahead, takes the stripe with the most room (ped_lateral_cost per metre aside, ped_keep_right_cost per metre off its own track, a better one only ped_stripe_gain_m better and after ped_stripe_hold_s), steps aside at ped_lateral_share of its pace and keeps ped_gap_m plus ped_headway_s behind a body (ped_accel to speed up again). The same stripes everywhere they walk: each walker sees every body near it (walkers in any mode, the street furniture's footprints) remapped into its own way's frame (SUMO's walking areas), on a sidewalk, round a corner (as wide either side of its line as the sidewalk it heads for, closing toward a place it must reach as fast as it steps aside, the leftmost ped_reserve_share up to ped_reserve_max_m left to those coming the other way: SUMO's reserve-oncoming on walking areas) and over a zebra (its right half only); a body moving slower than ped_moving_ms (under a body's width in 4 s) stands, one heading against its own way comes the other way; held up ped_jam_s on a sidewalk or round a corner, ped_jam_crossing_s on a zebra and ped_jam_narrow_s where its way holds one stripe only (SUMO jamtime 300 s, jamtime.crossing 10 s, jamtime.narrow 1 s) it squeezes past walkers (never furniture) at ped_jam_share of its pace (SUMO: a quarter). At a crosswalk the waiting stand on their own right half of the zebra, kerb_wait_gap_m apart within kerb_wait_half_m of its middle, in up to kerb_wait_rows rows back from the kerb (as many as leave a way along the sidewalk), step forward when a place ahead frees and cross from that place. Walkers appear on the sidewalks whose middle lies within ped_window_m of the camera and are taken away past ped_despawn_window_share of it: the 120 m beyond a 600 m window are half the longest segment (tuning road.max_seg_m, 112 m: 56 m) plus the 64 m the camera moves before the window is looked at again (traffic/window.cpp), so no walker is taken away at the edge it was just put on. Read by native/src/api/traffic_loader.cpp into TrafficParams. Distances in metres, times in seconds, speeds in m/s unless the key says km/h.
